issues.legal_issue: A tenant breaches a lease term requiring premises to be used for the tenant’s residence with family members when the tenant stops living there and family members continue to occupy it as a separate unit.
material_facts: A government employee was allotted a two-room flat under a tenancy agreement requiring the premises to be used exclusively as the residence of the tenant and the members of his family.
The tenant later moved with his wife to another leased flat and stopped residing in the allotted premises.
The tenant’s elder brother and two unmarried sisters continued to occupy the allotted premises.

The prescribed authority issued a notice on the ground that the tenant’s cessation of occupation violated the lease term and automatically terminated the tenancy under section 3(2) of the West Bengal Government Premises (Tenancy Regulation) Act, 1976.
The High Court’s Division Bench held that the lease term was not violated because a member of the tenant’s family continued to live in the premises.
issues.conclusion: The tenant violated the lease term when he ceased to occupy the premises himself. The tenancy therefore stood automatically terminated under section 3(2); the appeal was allowed, the Division Bench judgment was set aside, and the Single Judge’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(2) of the West Bengal Government Premises (Tenancy Regulation) Act, 1976, a tenancy automatically terminates when the tenant violates a lease term. The lease wording that the premises be used for the residence of the tenant and the members of his family requires the tenant to reside there with family members; it does not allow family members to continue occupying the premises as a separate unit after the tenant leaves. Baldev Sahai Bangia v. R.C. Bhasin, [1982] 3 SCR 670, was distinguished because the Delhi Rent Control Act provision there referred to neither the tenant nor any family member residing in the premises, wording capable of applying where either one remained.

rule.if: government_tenancy_appeal and residential_use_condition and tenant_ceased_residence and family_occupied_separately

predicates.government_tenancy_appeal: The dispute came before the court as an appeal concerning a tenancy of premises owned by government.
predicates.residential_use_condition: The tenancy agreement required the premises to be used as the residence of the tenant and the tenant’s family members.
predicates.tenant_ceased_residence: The tenant stopped living in the premises and lived elsewhere.
predicates.family_occupied_separately: Family members continued living in the premises without the tenant as a separate household.
predicates.lease_term_violated: The tenant’s conduct violated the lease term governing residential use.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning a government-premises tenancy, when the agreement requires the tenant and family members to reside in the premises, the tenant leaves, and family members remain there separately, the lease term is violated.
